newsitem.title: LATVIA: O/N RATES SEEN FALLING, LAT IN DEMAND.
newsitem.headline: O/N RATES SEEN FALLING, LAT IN DEMAND.

text.p: High overnight rates were seen falling but demand for lats was expected to remain high as big foreign investors come to the market, dealers said.
Overnight rates eased slightly from a bid/ask of 4.50/5.50 percent at mid-week to 4.00/5.00 percent as banks rectified their liquidity situations.
"There's been a big demand for lats out there and that has kept rates higher than usual and made the market very active...about 15 million lats per day over the past two weeks," said one dealer.
"But overnight rates won't stay high much longer, and should fall before the end of the month," he added.
Demand for lats was keeping the lat/dollar rate near the central bank intervention rate on Friday. The interbank rates were 0.5756/76 while the central bank rates were 0.5754/870.

Aside from banks' needs to meet liquidity requirements, dealers said other factors behind the demand for lats included company tax obligations and foreign investors looking to invest in lat-denominated debt.
They added that the demand for lats was expected to stay high as the market anticipates Russia's Gazprom will soon enter the market.
"Gazprom hasn't paid for its stake in Latvian Gas yet, but it is expected to come soon," said one dealer.
In the debt market this week, demand fell and short-term T-bill yields edged up.
"Banks are now finding other places to invest their money...Unfortunately, the money won't be channeled into equities," said one broker.
